tips.comment: Sportingsilvermine is in solid nick and looks dangerous here. Won twice recently and wasn’t disgraced at Newmarket last time in a deeper race. Handles different surfaces, travels well in his races, and this drop in class should suit.

Has a problem with starting slow and playing catch-up. If the added visor for the first time helps with this, Appier should be a threat. 2nd of 5 last time out, running on over CD, after usual slow start to be beaten by 3/4 lengths by in-form Odin Legacy. Off same mark and so may go close.
Sawgrass has been a beaten favourite on her last two runs but is given another chance to get her first win going up in distance again, Hugh Morrison does well with his stayers.
Black Smoke evidently remains in form, and this looks like an open enough race, which may fall into the hands of this horse.

The Colorist, a 5-year-old bay gelding by Time Test trained by Karen Jewell, contests tomorrow’s 1m6f Class 6 handicap at Lingfield, with David Probert retained in the saddle . A rare blend of consistency and back-marker speed, he’s recorded three wins and a series of credible finishes, including seconds and thirds on turf and AW.
His recent form reads 3??'2??'7??'2??'4 from his last five outings, showing you can’t write him off . His latest effort came over the same 1m6f trip here, running a solid yet unlucky fourth, just two lengths behind. That effort hints he’s fit, well-handicapped, and ready to bounce.
Lingfield’s flat mile-and-a-half gauge and Probert’s tactical steering set him up for a strong late surge. Off a mark of 58, he deserves consideration, especially if the pace up front is strong.

Wateen has been 2nd, beaten by three-quarters of a length in both her races so far. She looked slightly unlucky last time as she received a bump from the eventual winner midway through the race, which put her on the back foot, having a couple of lengths to make up. She did this by the final furlong, where she briefly led before Kamakameleon fought her off.

Was quite keen on SINJ yesterday, but connections withdrew. If anything, this is a more suitable trip, with breeding suggesting the softer going should suit. Hopefully, it does not get too much firmer, but even if it does, there's enough in previous runs to suggest she can land one sooner or later.

Daisy Roots is a consistent and well-handicapped runner in the 5:00 at Lingfield. With strong recent form (49-242) and running off a manageable weight, she looks ready to win. Jockey Pat Cosgrave is a positive booking, and the race conditions suit her perfectly. A solid win contender today.
City Of York won 3 times on the trot in 2023 and subsequently went up a lot in the handicap. Has had 2 promising runs since his break and is now lower than the first of those 3 wins.

Colinski is likely to show considerably more now in this low-grade handicap. Hector Crouch is booked today after going off at 80 in both of the latest starts and being always behind as well. Hoping for a good start here.
I like this horse as a complete unknown at this trip. Looking at the pedigree, it should be well suited. It's a weak race and has been well supported in the market.
Emily Rebecca is probably better at ten furlongs but fought back well after getting passed last time and should at least get placed at Lingfield.

Steadily improving MAUNDY THURSDAY could be ready to strike before too long. Last two runs on the turf have been stamped with winners so can potentially be marked up and I think she could benefit from a slight drop in trip too. We're in three year-old territory and there's plenty of early handicappers in here, so don't go overboard but there's definitely each-way claims with any further improvement.
Handicap debut showed some promise in previous runs. Good jock-trainer combo. Trainer does fairly well at this course. Celtic Diligence has a fair opening mark.

Lightly raced maiden who showed some encouraging signs last time out when switching from all-weather to turf. She was 4th of 7 last month in what was her handicap debut, and with a dropped mark, she might just have a chance.
Makes Me Wonder won over a mile here at Yarmouth on his penultimate start and looked unlucky in running last time at Brighton when forced wide and not getting a clear run finishing in 3rd place.

Fallon won aboard two outings ago when saddling the 3-year-old for the first time, even though it was on Tapeta over 8 and a half furlongs. The filly returns to Yarmouth, for it was back in April that she finished midfield here then. Wiser this time, and despite not being the finished article and marked up by 1lb after the 4th last time out at Ripon over a mile, she goes down in trip by 1 furlong and should be in this.
Tipping 3-year-old filly Castellina to improve on her last run where she had a wide draw. Much better draw this afternoon, stall five, and should run well for trainer James Fanshaw. E/W.

This horse's close-up 4th in an AW Maiden last year when sent off 2nd fav provides a few clues that he could well be up to winning this off a mark of just 56 in only his 2nd handicap. Those ahead of him in that race are basically 70-75 type horses, so you'd have to say that the fact he was competitive in that race for so long, and was so fancied, suggests he's worth sticking with here. The jockey looked to give the horse somewhat of an 'educational' race last time out (which was also a seasonal debut run), and there could be much more to come now.

Chinkara is the pick of those fillies that have run. This will be the fourth race for her, having run three times at a mile. The drop in distance to 7f could get her first win, as she ran green 2f out last time at Windsor and made no further progress in the final furlong in 3rd place.

Heart Of Eternity is worth taking a chance against the favourite here. Chinkara has had three runs with only some appeal and Appleby has a very good record on this track so I think this one is the better option.

Rhythmic Acclaim looks to have an excellent chance here. She has a great record at the track. She's 4lb below her last winning mark and ran well in a much better race than this last time out. She drops to a class 6 here from class 4, and this looks like a poor race. She should have too much for these.

I’m putting up Coolagh Magic in the 15:45 at Yarmouth as an each-way play ??' think he’s really well set for this. He’s an old boy now at 9, but he’s holding his form really well and comes into this after a cracking second over course and distance last time out. That was off the same mark, and he looked like he was finishing strongest of all.
He’s won 9 times in his career and has loads of solid runs at this level, so we know he’s up to it. What I really like is how consistent he’s been lately ??' placed in a good few of his last runs and seems to run his race every time. Plus, he’s got a decent draw and should be able to sit handy before kicking on late.
The fact he’s back at Yarmouth, where he’s gone close recently, and with William Carson riding again, makes me think they’re expecting another good effort.
Backing him each-way ??' solid, honest type in the form to go close again.
Perianth is a distance winner who is stepping back in trip. 2 lb below last winning mark and was a solid 4th off 11 last time out at Doncaster. 6f and a flat track should suit. Each way player.
Likely to kick on a bit now handicapping and has a good draw for this sprint. Hollie Doyle on top to guide him. He has a chance to place in this with minimal improvement. E/W bet.
Beaten favorite in a 4-runner race at Leicester over 7f in soft ground and clearly didn't get home. Drops back in distance and was a winner in May at Beverley and debut run for new trainer.
Course and distance win and a career-best win at Newmarket last month over the mile. Repeat of that and will go close.
Second last time, given much too much to do. Distance no problem. Great apprentice on board and in form. Will be there at the business end of the race. Win bet.
Thrown into handicaps at the earliest opportunity, I think that Believe The Storm could be well handicapped here, with the aim to have this horse as a Saturday horse. Decent opportunity here.
Unassuming was a bit unlucky last time when favorite in a small race at Kempton. Coming back from a long break and has been well backed, so should be fit.

Class-dropping ATLANTIC GAMBLE drops to below last winning mark and with the stable generally performing very well here at Yarmouth, I think even as the yard's second string there are each-way claims if the new headgear does the trick. Jockey has won on board before and he could definitely outrun this price.

Unexposed 3yo filly, four career runs. She was 2nd of 11 two weeks ago on her handicap debut, no chance behind the winner - now rated 65 - but she had the measure of the rest. Improvement very possible, strong jockey booking and now facing much lower rated rivals in this 0-50 classified stakes.
Interesting jock booking on handicap debut. In a pretty poor race, it could be worth looking to an improver/unexposed type and a powerful jock booking.

This outsider is actually only 3lb off being top rated in this classified race and looks well overpriced at 16/1. She was staying on into 3rd over this trip just 2 starts ago when not getting the run of the race and she wasn't beaten far behind a couple of horses that have both won since. The drop back in trip didn't suit last time out but this could be ideal now with a jockey booked who knows this course well.

The 5-year-old is in good form. A narrow defeat during April. He shared a dead-heat win three weeks ago. Now dropping into a low-grade 0-50 level weights classified stakes. Weighted to run a big race but now has the added help of a good apprentice - 2 wins and a narrow defeat from his last 4 rides - and his 7lb claim should help.
In a field of pretty inconsistent horses, this horse's course and distance form sticks out, and Jack Doughty is in some form too. Good each way play.

I’m putting up Primrose Maid in the last at Yarmouth ??' she’s one who’s been bubbling under and looks ready to hit the frame again. She ran a solid race here just last week, finishing 3rd of 10 over this same 1m trip, staying on well late and showing she’s in decent heart.
She’s back at a track she clearly likes ??' her only career win came over 7f here last season ??' and this return to a mile suits her running style. The key angle here is Brandon Wilkie taking off a valuable 3lb, which puts her on a really nice racing weight. That can only help in a race of this nature.
She’s not the flashiest, but at this grade, she’s more than capable. With that recent third under her belt and coming back quickly in similar conditions, she’s got an each-way squeak for sure.
Each-way play ??' good recent form, back at her favoured track, and Wilkie’s claim puts her right in this.

Walson's Law looks ready to strike. He's been holding his form well on the all-weather, and the slight ease in the weights could be just what he needs. Back at Kempton where he's gone well before, he's drawn to get a handy position and looks primed to land one.

Lightly raced filly who bumped into one when running a good race here two starts ago. No show in 6f race last time out and opening mark looks generous in first time hood back to more suitable conditions.

Has not finished out of the first 3 in any of the last 12 starts. 5 of them were wins, all over 1 mile, 4 of which came on the AW. Finished second last time out behind today's forecast favorite Walsons Law, conceding 2 lbs to the winner. Has a 5 lbs pull with that horse today, so is entitled to get closer. Looks a big player again tonight.

Just four career runs from the 4yo. Back from a 7 month break with a win over this 8f C/D five weeks ago in an apprentice handicap - good RPR rating. Strong jockey change, only 2lb higher in the weights and room for plenty more improvement.

Berry Clever’s been bubbling under and looks set to go close. He’s a two-time winner at Kempton and has hit the frame on turf the last twice, so he’s clearly in decent nick. Back on a track he likes and off a fair mark, he’s definitely one to have onside.

Calanthe, a 4??'year??'old Kingman gelding trained by Archie Watson and ridden by Luke Morris, lines up with a rating of 71 in this 1-mile Class 5. He's dropped to a competitive mark and arrives in solid form.
He bagged a comfortable win at Lingfield on 28 April, making all under Hollie Doyle, and discounted the dreaded 3lb rise perfectly . He followed up with a close second at Kempton in mid??'April behind Norflondonforever, showing his liking for the surface . His latest run at Leicester (10 May) saw him finish fourth but confirm he’s holding form .
Calanthe is typically prominent early and well-suited to kicking on in the home straight. With his Polytrack prowess, and Morris steadying him throughout, he looks well placed to be involved.
Why I’m tipping him: recent win proven on AW, competitive staying power, and in-form trainer/rider combo make him a strong each-way option at double??'figure odds.

Let's just suppose MONOPOLISE needed the run last time out after over three months off. He now returns close to last winning mark and with some decent course and distance form in the locker is considered at this price. Could be a danger if bouncing back to last season's peak form.

With 7 horses, including my selection, making their debut, anything is possible in this race. But it's the sire, Ardad (IRE), that just might be the difference. He has a profitable record in the last 28 days, and the market suggests she has an outside chance.
This daughter of Frankel should improve significantly from her debut run last time when she was very green. Not knocked about and ran on well once the penny dropped late on.

Cloaks Of Gold looks a strong contender at Kempton. She shaped well on debut at Salisbury and the switch to the all-weather should suit given her pedigree. With that experience under her belt and a rider who knows her, she’s got every chance of going one better.

Bumper and fair hurdle champion. She has demonstrated some ability by placing in a couple of 1 and a half mile flat maidens this spring, yet she could be susceptible to advancing 3-year-olds in this event. However, Donald McCain is a savvy trainer, and Clifford Lee, who will be riding, is in excellent form. The odds of 80/1 are enticing for an each-way wager.

A Richard Hannon-trained 3-year-old who has had only 1 race on the all-weather, winning here at Kempton in May in a class 4 fillies' handicap over 6f, ridden by today's jockey Sean Levey, when making all to win by a neck. She is in a class 4 handicap over 6f. This filly finished 4th of 11 runners last time out at Haydock in a class 4 handicap over 6f on good going, where she got headed inside the final furlong, beaten 2 1/2 lengths by the favorite. She has won on the flat at Newbury over 6f on soft going. She is a course/distance winner with a 100% strike rate on the all-weather. Has an each-way shout in this race tonight.

Backspin looks ready to pounce at Kempton. He bolted up at Southwell two starts back and wasn’t far off at Lingfield last time despite not getting the cleanest run. The drop back to six furlongs could play to his strengths and he’s still on a workable mark.

Aparajeo has only run twice, which have been on turf. He won on course debut at Windsor over six furlongs in a class five race last July. Following that success, connections sent him to run in a group two race at Goodwood, which was way too strong for him, and he finished last. Today, he makes his all-weather debut at Kempton over six furlongs in a class four race. Providing he has wintered well and handles the surface, the handicapper appears to have given Aparajeo every chance of once again winning his first race of the season.

Habari has his first outing since leaving the ownership of the Aga Khan. More would have been expected from this half-brother to four winners, all of whom have shown a better standard of form. All outings have been over one mile but his dam won over 7 furlongs (from two career outings) and his sire Churchill is from a speedy family so the drop to sprint distance may suit. In front at today's distance on his latest outing in January, Habari has form on Polytrack. New handler Daragh Bourke is in form and travels from Scotland for this.

My vote to take this class 6 handicap will going to the Rock Of Gibralter colt Cloudside Rock who was last seen at this venue at the 1 mile 3 furlong 219 yards trip where finishing a very creditable 3rd/12 and was unlucky not to finish closer as he was denied a clear run entering the final 2 furlongs and was forced to switch right once in clear he kept on with promise and did his best under those circumstances currently operating on an unchanged mark of 57 David Simcock's inmate looks poised to strike here and in my point of view this 4yo is open to the most progress in field and he is the least exposed in the field drop back down in trip racing at the 1 mile 2 furlong 219 yards trip that being of no concern jockey Kieren Shoemark takes the ride and can give Cloudside Rock a promising ride here at Kempton must be considered

Both good runs came on the AW, and both poor ones on turf, including at Carlisle last time. Too much use was made of him there, and he will do better back to waiting tactics, especially in a field where there looks to be plenty of pace.

Ignac Lamar has won two of his last four races including last time over course and distance when he was a pound out of the handicap. He is up four pounds still on a lowly mark of 50 and top amateur Simon Walker has been booked to ride so should follow up against slightly better opposition.

Better And Better was an unfancied 20-1 when just denied in 2nd place in a three-way photo over 5f at Carlisle. He travelled strongly all the way on a stiff track and should cope with the extra furlong against Try Storm Cat who finished 3rd over 6f at Pontefract after leading.

This looks like a penalty kick for Valiancy, trained by William Haggas, against a fairly weak field of maidens. He was 2nd, beaten by half a length last time at Haydock despite a slow start. That was a big improvement and the best form on offer here.

Parisiac loves it at Hamilton. He won his penultimate race here by a nose off 66 and then ran here with a five-pound penalty, finishing 2nd off 71. Now he is three pounds well in, running off 68, and Mohammed Tabti rides, taking off a useful five pounds.

Winged Messenger's seasonal reappearance was a decent one. Although the subsequent form from it is not great, those horses are rated much higher than this lot. Great chance if building on that comeback.

Is a previous course and distance winner. Was looking like the winner of a race 14 days ago before weakening out of it and finishing last. A repeat of that but seeing out the race better and should be winning a race of this nature. Solid chance for an in-form trainer in Ruth Carr.

Lady Celia was going well at this time of year last season with wins at the end of May and the first half of July. 5 furlongs is this mare's distance and she has won on good and soft going. Lady Celia is two pounds lower on official ratings compared to her success over course and distance in July. Shay Farmer takes over in the saddle claiming a useful seven pounds allowance.

French Haven won by half a length at Newmarket off a mark of 60 and then finished 2nd, beaten a neck off 62 at Nottingham, both times ridden by Jamie Spencer. Those were improved performances. Her previous jockey, Joe Fanning, takes over and should be able to continue the improved form on 62, one pound ahead of the handicapper.

Shahnaz was the winner of this 12 months ago albeit off a slightly lower mark but has every chance of following up. Only one start this year when 6th of 11 again over course and distance. That should hopefully have her spot on and she has a great each way chance.

CISCO DISCO's disappointing run last time out has served to drop the handicap mark and will hopefully have tuned him up for this one. Now 2 lbs below last season's peak run at Ayr, so might be able to get in the frame if in the mood. Has been more miss than hit lately, but still can't be totally ruled out.
Ran his best race of the year last time and would have finished closer with a clear run. Worth a bet from just a pound higher here.
Solid enough efforts the last 2 runs. Same mark here, so runs off 63. Solid each-way chance at a track the horse has run well in the past.

Gracesolution showed reasonably well with a middle-of-the-pack 5th of 11 finish last time out at Gowran Park in an encouraging first outing of the year away from the all-weather. The stable did well in going at a slightly longer distance of 1m6f, which should make this drop back to 1m3½f all the more favorable, and is a previous winner at this distance.

War Correspondent is back on the flat after a hurdles campaign, which was able to snag a win, which is more than most of these have been capable of. Playing safe here, I think the jockey booking means business today, so winning would be the bonus but should be in the frame.

Expound mixes hurdling and flat well and has won his last two races in May on the flat at Ballinrobe, making all by a nose. He followed that with a win over hurdles at Clonmel. With a three-pound rise in his mark, he could make it three wins in a row.

A 6 times career winner between 7f and 1 mile whose last win came over 7f at Naas last summer. Back in good form after a strong staying on third over 6f at Listowel 10 days ago and is likely to be better suited by this step up in trip to 1 mile.
Not out of the frame in her last four races . Not beaten far when runner-up at Gowran Park earlier this month and can go one better with the drop in trip here.

KATIE ROSS wears a changed headgear combination for a new dual-purpose yard. She races in open-age handicap company as a three year old filly which could suit with sufficient experience and this yard have no issues getting one ready following an absence.

Still a maiden after 8 career starts but has shown promise in both starts this year. Only beaten 2.25 lengths last time out when 5th of 20 runners over 1 mile at Naas at the end of April. That effort can be marked up as did not enjoy the clearest passage that day and should run well.

CHOU CHOU clearly on a favourable mark could be showing all the right signs back at the yard of this small outfit. Connections have clearly done well to secure the services of champion jockey Colin Keane and with two reappearance sighters behind him the market could confirm he is ready now.

I've ended up with pie on my face more than once, but dare I say that Tom McCourt’s four-year-old gelding CELTIC DRUID could be inching a little closer to minor money here. He lines up fresh off his best run to date at Roscommon last month (7f, good), where he finished fifth in a first-time visor - which is retained today. This son of CHURCHILL is effectively 3lb out of the handicap, but the booking of talented jockey Robert Whearty, whose 3lb claim negates that discrepancy, could make all the difference. It could certainly help to have a more experienced rider in the saddle this time.
Tom McCourt has a 25% place strike rate at Limerick over the last five years, and a return to the 7f trip - where he ran his best race in maiden company at Gowran Park - looks a positive move. The headgear remains on, and while CELTIC DRUID still has to prove himself, the signs of progress at Roscommon suggest he might not be far off. At 25/1, I'm happy to take a small, tentative play in the hope he can sneak into the frame in what doesn't look the deepest of contests.

This distance champion slightly faltered last season, having gone 14 races without a victory since 2024. After an 8-month break, if he returns in good shape for his season opener, with a beneficial 10 lb jockey's claim, then a 40/1 bet could yield a profit from an each-way wager.
Joseph O'Brien and JP McManus have got into the habit of cleaning up these longer distance races, and this represents another good opportunity for the combination to strike again.

QUIZ TEST punted on his recent return should be ready now. His quick enough turnaround clearly reads well and Shane Foley takes the ride on this five year old from his further reduced mark. Looking feasibly treated now likely to stay he should go close.

A 4 times winner, 3 times on the flat and once over hurdles. Stays well and won twice last year between July and September. No show the last two times, but they were in better races than this and will be better suited by this step up in trip, so could go well dropped in class.

JR MAHON could prove well placed and well handicapped starting out life in this sphere from a mark of 69. The Jess Harrington yard have just found their way approaching the summer festivals and this potential big improver by notable sire Wooton Bassett looks interesting.

Jéssica Harrington’s INVIGORATED should improve now she’s handicapping. She’s had her 3 maiden spins without showing a whole pile. She did, however, run well without showing her hand, given a hands and heels ride on her 2nd maiden on good ground. Up in trip today, back on a sound surface, and with Harrington’s stable flying, I’ll take a chance on her 2nd string can step forward.
The Adrian McGuinness-trained Sottsass has better form than most in this field and could go well at a price here under a positive ride from Adam Caffrey.
Tired towards the finish last time out over a mile and a quarter at the Curragh but can make amends here returning to a mile.

Profitable filly. Half-sister to 2-year-old 6f winner Princ X J, she has a strong pedigree. Her dam achieved victory at 1m with trainer O'Callaghan. The O'Callaghan stable is thriving, and the jockey's 3lb claim may offer an edge. An each-way wager at 28/1 appears to be a wise choice.

Consistent handicapper now back to last winning mark. Proven at the distance and versatile regarding ground. While he hasn’t won in some time, he's often thereabouts and may benefit from the drop in trip. Wide draw is a concern, but he's a solid place chance if handling conditions.

TOFINO could be well placed at the foot of the weights by ace dual-purpose trainer Gavin Cromwell. The yard have kept ticking over nicely through the change-over months and reappearing in Claiming company latest this filly taking in her first handicap as a three year old could be well treated.

A 3-time winner between 1 mile and 1m2f, the last one coming at Ballinrobe last July. Makes first start for 9 months here but only finished 0.5 lengths when second in this race on first run last year, so looks capable of a big run today.

Horses for courses pick here with Church Mountain. Has won this race before in 2022 and won again over C & D in April. Last two races very much under par, so I'm hoping a return here, even with this draw, can spring him back to life.

HELIOGABALUS is a runner who has an experinced jockey aboard for the first time as a four year old. He may have developed considerably through the off-season and could be ready to show his hand in this sphere from his now career-low mark.
Big Baby Bull has sunk down the ratings and comes to Limerick today, where this horse has won before. Worth an each-way go here.

IN THE MINUS could prove a well treated three year old now looking like he may have come to hand. Sire Belardo produces plenty with higher ratings than this racer and his high draw may prove suitable drawn away from inside traffic when turning right.

JASMINE AFFANALIS is an intruiging outsider with this shrewd trainer not having many in his yard rated this low. That could mean this filly is ready to get competritive tonight and having shown more switched to turf for her recent return run she makes each-way appeal.
